title: HR 违规解雇与 PIP 纠纷

sources.title: 29 U.S.C. § 2101 — WARN Act Definitions (Cornell LII)
sources.key_facts: Employer threshold: 100 full-time employees OR 100+ employees working ≥4,000 hours/week (excl. overtime). Plant closing: ≥50 employees (excl. part-time) within any 30-day period. Mass layoff: ≥33% of workforce AND ≥50 employees, OR ≥500 employees (excl. part-time), within any 30-day period. Part-time defined as <20 hours/week average OR <6 of 12 preceding months employed.

sources.title: What is the WARN Act? — Thomson Reuters Legal
sources.key_facts: 60 calendar days advance written notice required. Civil penalty: up to $500/day for failure to notify local government (avoidable if employees paid within 3 weeks). Damages: back pay and benefits for up to 60 days for affected employees.

sources.title: Cal-WARN Act — California Department of Industrial Relations Official Page
sources.key_facts: 60 days advance written notice required. Employer liability for non-compliance: back pay and benefits up to max of 60 days or one-half the number of days employed. Notices must include federal WARN Act elements. Cal-WARN applies to employers with ≥75 employees at any point in past 12 months (Labor Code §§ 1400–1408).

sources.title: California WARN Act Thresholds — Shouse Law Group
sources.key_facts: Employer threshold: ≥75 employees (past 12 months). Mass layoff trigger: ≥50 employees within 30 days (NO 33% rule requirement unlike federal). Plant closure: cessation of business activities. Relocation: move ≥100 miles. Notice period: 60 days. Federal vs Cal-WARN comparison table confirmed.

sources.title: NY WARN Act FAQ — New York Department of Labor
sources.key_facts: Employer threshold: 50+ full-time employees (or 50+ including part-time working ≥2,000 hours/week aggregate). Plant closing trigger: ≥25 employees (excl. part-time) within 30 days. Mass layoff: ≥25 employees representing ≥33% of workforce, OR ≥250 employees (excl. part-time). Temporary layoffs <6 consecutive months excluded.

sources.title: NY WARN Act 2023 Amendments — Cooley Law
sources.key_facts: Notice period: 90 days (exceeds federal 60-day requirement). Employer threshold: 50+ full-time employees within New York State. 2023 amendment: remote workers based at NY employment site now count toward threshold. Enhanced disclosure: job titles, ages, compensation, union status, severance package info required. Expanded notice recipients: local government, school districts, emergency service providers.

sources.title: PIPs: Write, Implement and Time Them Precisely — SHRM
sources.key_facts: Recommended PIP duration: 30–90 days (30-day minimum per industry standard). Required PIP elements: specific measurable objectives, support/training provided, regular meeting schedule, stated consequences including potential termination, prior improvement opportunities documented. Immediate termination appropriate for: serious misconduct, insubordination, unlawful conduct, safety threats.

sources.title: Time Limits for Filing an EEOC Charge — EEOC Official
sources.key_facts: Standard deadline: 180 calendar days from date of discrimination. Extended deadline: 300 calendar days if a state or local agency enforces a law prohibiting employment discrimination on the same basis. ADEA: 300-day extension only if state law AND state agency prohibits age discrimination. EPA: 2 years (3 years for willful violations), no EEOC charge required. Federal employees: 45 days to contact EEO Counselor.

sources.title: EEOC: Q&A on OWBPA Severance Waivers
sources.key_facts: Individual termination: ≥21 days consideration period. Group layoff/RIF: ≥45 days consideration period. Revocation period: 7 days after signing (irrevocable, cannot be waived by agreement). Group disclosure required: decisional unit definition, eligibility factors, time limits, job titles and individual ages of all selected/non-selected employees. Material changes restart the 21/45-day clock.

sources.title: 5 CFR § 432.105 — Federal PIP Performance-Based Action (Cornell LII)
sources.key_facts: Federal agencies must provide 30-day advance notice of proposed action (extensible up to additional 30 days for medical evaluation, travel, disability accommodation, MSPB stays). Employee rights: opportunity to answer orally/in writing, representation by attorney, furnish medical documentation, receive final written decision within 30 days after notice expires. Performance instances must occur within 1-year period ending on date of notice.

sources.title: Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967 — EEOC Official
sources.key_facts: Protected age: ≥40 years old (no upper limit). Employer threshold: 20+ employees for each working day in 20+ calendar weeks. Prohibited: discharge because of age, wage reduction to comply with age requirements. OWBPA severance waiver requirements (group termination): 45-day consideration, job titles and ages of all program participants, 7-day revocation.

sources.title: 29 CFR § 825.110 — FMLA Eligible Employee (Cornell LII)
sources.key_facts: Three-part eligibility test: (1) employed ≥12 months (need not be consecutive); (2) ≥1,250 hours of service in preceding 12-month period; (3) worksite where employer has ≥50 employees within 75 miles. Employer coverage: private employers with 50+ employees in 20+ workweeks in current or preceding calendar year. Leave entitlement: up to 12 weeks unpaid, job-protected leave per year.

sources.title: Montana WDEA § 39-2-904 — MT Legislature Official
sources.key_facts: Montana is the only state with statutory limits on at-will employment for private employers. Termination requires 'good cause' after probationary period. Default probationary period: 12 months (max 18 months). Lost wages remedy capped at 4 years from discharge date. Employer policy violations constitute wrongful discharge only when materially depriving employee of fair opportunity to maintain employment.
